Extension of Mid-day Meal Scheme 
*522. SHRI KB. KRISHNA MURTHY: Will the Minister of HUMAN 
RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Karnataka Government has sought more grants to extend 
the Mid-day Meal Scheme upto the tenth standard; 
(b) if so, the amount of additional grants sought for; 
(c) the number of children to be benefited as a result thereof; and 
(d) the present status of the above proposal? 
THE MINISTER OF HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT (SHRI 
ARJUN SINGH): (a) No, Sir. 
(b) to (d) Do not arise in view of (a) above. 
SHRI KB. KRISHNA MURTHY: Sir, regarding the questions that I have 
put, technically speaking, I am satisfi ed with the answer. But I have a 
supplementary. 
In 2001-02, the Ministry of Human Resource Development had 
accumulated arrears, payable to the Food Co rporation of India, to the tune of 
crores of rupees on account of foodgrains supplied by the FCI for the 
 
 
1 

RAJYA SABHA  [2 May, 2005] 
Mid-day Meal Scheme, and the FCI had to discontinue the foodgrains supply 
to the Mid -day Meal Scheme to put pressure on the HRD Ministry to pay up. 
A public interest litigation was filed in the Apex Court. Though the FCI had 
an air-tight claim, the Co urt, on compassionate ground, considering school-
going children's nutrition and hunger, ordered resumption of foodgrains 
supply by the FCI. I want to know whether, presently, the HRD Ministry 
promptly settles the claims of the FCI for the supply of foodgrains to the Mid-
day Meal Scheme. 
SHRI ARJUN SINGH: Sir, so far as the present Scheme is concerned, 
there is no such hiatus that has come to our knowledge. Whatever happened 
in the past, we are trying to see that it is sorted out. At present, there is 
nothing like that. 
SHRI K.B. KRISHNAMURTHY: Sir, the Planning Commission has 
asked the States to earmark 15 per cent of the Central assistance under 
PMGRY for meeting the cooking expenses under the Mid-day Meal Scheme. 
Is it being excluded by the State? 
SHRI ARJUN SINGH: Sir, that compon ent has now been included in the 
Mid-day Meal Scheme that we are implementing and it has been raised from 
Re. 1 to Rs. 2. 
SHRI PG. NARAYANAN: Mr. Chairman, Sir, Tamil Nadu has been 
implementing the Mid-day Meal Scheme for the school-going children for the 
past 35 years. I would like to know from the hon. Minister the assistance 
given by the Centre to this massive programme. Considering the fact that 
Tamil Nadu is a pioneer State in implementing this Scheme, will the Central 
Government come forward to bear the entire cost of this Scheme? 
SHRI ARJUN SINGH: Sir, I may point out that this extension of the Mid-
day Meal Scheme refers to the second ary stage and the answer is to that 
question. In the case of primary stage, I think, the Government of India has 
made itself very clear. 
SHRI JAIRAM RAMESH: Sir, I would lik e to ask the hon. Minister that 
the Mid-day Meal Scheme was introduced with great expectations. Although 
my question is not strictly dealing with Karnataka, I would still like to ask, 
based on the current assessment, in whic h of the States the Minister thinks 
that the Mid-day Meal Scheme has taken off. I would like to know whether 
he is prepared to devote greater amount of managerial and financial resources 
to get this Scheme off the ground in those laggard States. 
 
 
2 

[2 May, 2005] RAJYA SABHA 
Which are the laggard States where the Mid-day Meal Scheme is not making 
an impact? 
SHRI ARJUN SINGH: It would be unfair to call any State 'laggard'. So far 
as the present scheme is concerned, all the States are showing enthusiasm 
and, I think, we should bear with them. That is all I can say.

Promotion of Urdu language in Bihar 
*524. SHRI MOTIUR RAHMAN: Will the Minister of HUMAN 
RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
(a) whether Urdu is second language in Bihar; 
(b) if so, what steps are being taken to promote Urdu in the State; 
(c) whether Government are aware that examination papers of different State 
level examinations are not made available in Urdu; and 
(d) if so, the steps being taken in this regard? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HUMAN RESOURCE 
DEVELOPMENT (SHRI MD. ALI ASHRAF FATMI): (a) to (d) A Statement is 
laid on the Table of the Sabha. 
Statement 
(a) Yes, Sir. 
(b) According to the Government of Bihar the following steps have been taken 
by the State to promote the Urdu language: 
(i) A separate Urdu Directorate has been constituted under the Department 
of Raj Bhasha by the Government of Bihar. 
*Not recorded. 
5 
[2 May, 2005] 

RAJYA SABHA [2 May, 2005] 
(ii) An Urdu Advisory Committee has been constituted to advise the State 
Government regarding development and extension of the second Raj Bhasha, 
Urdu, 
(Hi) An Urdu Magazine "Urdu Patrika Sangam" is published by the State 
Government, 
(iv) Seminars and Conferences are organized on Urdu Diwas every year for 
promotion of the Urdu lanugage, 
(v) Steps have been taken to translate Government Rules & Regulations in Urdu, 
(vi) Applications in Urdu are entertained in Government Offices, 
(vii) The State Government honours Urdu Scholars, Journalist and others under 
the'Urdu PuraskarYojana', 
(viii) Urdu Translators and Typists have been appointed by the Government in Field 
Offices all over the State, 
(ix) Students of class X and XII in Bihar have the option to write the answers in 
their examinations in Hindi, English and Urdu. 
Apart from the steps taken by the Government of Bihar to promote the Urdu lanugage, 
the Central Government also promotes the Urdu language under various Centrally 
sponsored schemes and through the National Council for Promotion of the Urdu 
Language (NCPUL) an autonomous organization supported by the Central 
Government. Under the Central scheme for appointment of Language teachers, Central 
assistance is provided for appointment of Urdu teachers in primary and upper primary 
schools in educationally backward minority blocks. During the year 2004-05, an 
amount of Rs. 43.20 lakhs have been released to the Government of Bihar for 
appointment of 360 Urdu teachers. 
(c) and (d) Yes, Sir. 
All the question papers are set in Hindi and English. However, the students have the 
option to write their answers in Urdu. The replies submitted in Urdu are checked by subject 
specialists with the help of Urdu experts.

National Capital Region Board 
*531. SHRI DATTA MEGHE: Will the Minister of URBAN 
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
(a) when the National Capital Region Board was constituted; 
(b) the composition of the Board; 
(c) the terms and reference of the Board; 
(d) the amount spent so far by the Board; 
(e) whether the Board has failed in achieving its objectives; 
(f) if so, the reasons therefor; and 
(g) the measures taken by Government to develop the NCR towns so as to 
reduce pressure of population in Delhi? 
THE MINISTER OF URBAN DEVELOPMENT (SHRI GHULAM NABI 
AZAD): (a) The National Capital Region Planning Board (NCRPB) was 
constituted on 28.3.1985 as per the provisions of National Capital Region 
Planning Board'Act, 1985. 
(b) The National Capital Region Planning Board comprises of 21 
Members and 10 Co-opted Members. A list of Members of the Board is 
enclosed as a Statement (See below). 
(c) The National Capital Region Planning Board is responsible for 
preparation of a Plan for development of the National Capital Region and for 
coordinating and monitoring the implementation of such plan for evolving 
harmonized policies for the control of land-use and development of 
infrastructure in the National Capital Region so as to avoid any haphazard 
development of the region and for matters incidental thereto. 
(d) The National Capital Region Planning Board has informed that a total 
amount of Rs. 1983.78 crore has been released so far in the form of interest 
bearing loan to the Governments of the participating States in the 
33 

RAJYA SABHA [2 May, 2005] 
NCR, their implementing agencies and to the Counter Magnet Areas for 
implementation of various projects. 
(e) and (f) It is difficult to quantify the achievements vis-a-vis the 
objectives of the National Capital Region Planning Board. However, the 
effect of planning and development of an area in a regional context can be 
infrerred on empirical evidence that the rate of growth of population of 
National Capital Territory of Delhi has declined to 47.02% in the decade 
1991-2001, as compared to the decennial growth rate of 52.44%, 52.99%, 
53% and &1.45%inthedecades1951-61,1961-71,1971-81,1981-91 
respectively. 
(g) Development of six Delhi Metropolitan Area (DMA) towns and 11 
Priority towns for absorbing Delhi bound migrants were envisaged in the 
Regional Plan-2001. Five Counter Magnet Areas were also identified. For 
development of infrastructure facilities in these areas, such as water supply, 
power, sewerage and drainage and roads and also creation of residential, 
industrial and commercial facilities so as to provide a boost to growth and 
development of these towns, the Board has provided loan assistance for 
implementation of projects. So far the Board has approved 200 projects at an 
estimated cost of Rs. 8047.65 crores and loan component of Rs. 4253.72 
crores. 101 projects have already been  completed while 83 projects are at 
different stages of implementation. 16 projects were subsequently withdrawn. 
NCRPB has also facilitated preparation of project proposals intended to 
enhance connectivity in the Region such as Eastern and Western Peripheral 
Expressway, Integrated Rail-cum-Bus Transit System.

532. SHRI S.S. AHLUWALIA: Will the Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE 
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
(a) whether a substantial positive growth in illiterate population aged 7 
years and above has been observed in so me of the districts in various States 
showing exception to the over all positiv e growth trends in literacy in the 
country as well as in the respective States; 
(b) if so, the details of such districts with positive growth of illiterate 
alongwith the growth rate of literacy of the concerned States; 
(c) the reasons for such exceptions in respective districts; and 
(d) the details of the steps, if any, bein g taken to reverse the trend in those 
districts? 
THE MINISTER OF HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT (SHRI 
ARJUN SINGH): (a) and (b) According to 2001 Census, the literacy rate of 
the country was 64.84% which shows an increase of 12.63% since 1991. All 
States/Union Territories have shown an increase in the literacy rates during 
1991-2001, thedetails of which are en closed in Statement-! (See below). The 
absolute number of non-literates has decreased for the first time by 24.06 
million. Despite the growth in the literacy rates in all States and Union 
Territories, 132 out of 593 districts have shown an increase in the number of 
illiterates as per Census 2001, the details of which are enclosed in Statement-
ll (See below). 
(c) The reasons for increase in the number of illiterates in these districts 
include growth in population, poverty, migration, socio-economic factors and 
lack of awareness about relevance of education. 
(d) The Universalisation of Elementary Education and eradication of adult 
illiteracy form the two-pronged strategy for improving the literacy rate of the 
country. Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan (SSA) is a comprehensive programme for 
universalizing quality Elementary Education by 2010. 
The National Literacy Mission (NLM) is also entrusted with the task of 
eradication of adult illiteracy in the coun try. The target of NLM is to achieve 
a sustainable 75% literacy rate by 2007. The thrust areas of NLM are 
improving female literacy in low female literacy areas, organizing projects for 
residual illiteracy in districts which have substantial number of illiterates, 
setting up of continuing education centres for providing opportunities for life-
long learning to the neo-literates and imparting vocational training to neo-
literates through Jan Shikshan Sansthans. Special programmes for Residual 
illiteracy have been taken up in the low female literacy districts

4035. SHRI RAJKUMAR DHOOT: Will the Minister of HEAVY 
INDUSTRIES AND PUBLIC ENTERPRISES be pleased to state:

conform to Euro-Ill standard; and

THE MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF HEAVY INDUSTRIES AND 
PUBLIC ENTERPRISES (SHRI SONTOSH MOHAN DEV): (a) and (b) As per

registered in the 11 (eleven) mega cities namely NCR of Delhi, Mumbai, Kolkata, Chennai,

† 4049. SHRI JANESHWAR MISHRA: Will the Minister of HUMAN 
RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that as a result of existing education system and commercialisation 
thereof tragedy like suicide among students has arisen due to increasing competition among

† Original notice of the question was received in Hindi. 
 
72

 
[2May, 2005] RAJYA SABHA 
(bj if so, the details thereof; 
(c) whether it is also a fact that our education system and prevailing defects in 
evaluation system are primarily behind this tendency; and 
(d) IT so, the measures being taken by Government to check this tendency? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HUMAN RESOURCE 
DEVELOPMENT (SHRI M,D. ALIASHRAF FATMI): (a) to (d) The problem of 
increasing stress among students during examinations and instances of some students 
committing suicides due to failure in examination and stress have been engaging the 
attention of the Government. However, there are various contributory factors such as 
competition, peer and parental pressure, fast changing socio and economic conditions, lack of 
employment opportunities and fear of failure in examinations which become the cause of 
tragedies like suicides among students. 
The Ministry is deeply concerned with the issue of high stress level among students 
caused by the public examinations at the end of class X and XII conducted by various boards, 
Joint Entrance Examinations for NTs and other entrance examinations. To address the 
question of promoting equality in access to education as also allow the students to have a 
stress free environment of joyful learning, the Ministry had convened a meeting recently 
with Eminent Educationists, Principals, representatives from premier institutions such as 
the Indian Institutes of Technology and Indian Institutes of Management, Heads of the Boards 
of Examination and others. It was unanimously agreed that there must be systemic reforms to 
eliminate exam-related stress. It was also felt that a national consensus on the issue 
should be reached through wider discussion.

RAJYA SABHA [2 May, 2005] 
Funds allocated to centrally run educational institutions 
4068. SHRI T.T.V. DHINAKARAN: Will the Minister of HUMAN 
RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
(a) the details of the funds allocated for the Centrally run educational institutions 
during the last three years, State-wise; 
(b) whether Government have any proposal to open more educational institutions 
including the schools during the Tenth Five year Plan period; and 
(c) if so, the details thereof? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN  THE MINISTRY OF HUMAN 
RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT (SHRI MD. ALI ASHRAF FATMI): (a) In 
many of the cases, funds are not allocated  by the Government directly to the 
centrally administered educational institutions. The Kendrya Vidyalayas (KVs) 
and Navodaya Vidyalayas (NVs) are administered by the Kendirya Vidyalaya 
Sangathan and Navodaya Vidyalaya Samiti respectively, for which central allocations 
are made. The Central Tibtan School Administration (CTSA) runs, manages and 
assists institutions set up for the education of Tibtan children in the country. 
Similarly, funds are allocated to University Grants Commission, which, in turn, 
distributes the funds to the various Universities/Colleges including the Central 
Universities. For institutions like Indian Institute of Technology (IITs). Indian 
Institutes of Managements (IIMs), National Institute of Technology (NIT) etc. 
block allocations are made, and funds are allocated to individual institutions 
based on their requirements and availability of resources. A Statement indicating the 
scheme-wise Annual Plan allocation (Budget Estimate), for the major centrally 
administered educational institutions/schemes, during the years 2003-04 to 
2005-06 is enclosed as a Statement (See below). 
(b) and (c) Expansion and opening of new educational institutions is a 
continuous process. The major proposals during the Tenth Five Year Plan include 
setting up of new KVs and NVs, a new Indian Institute of Management (IIM) in the 
North-Eastern Region and a Central Institute of Technology in Kckrajhar.

 RAJYA SABHA [2 May, 2005] 
External financial assistance for promotion of education 
4069. PROF. M.M. AGARWAL: Will the Minister of HUMAN 
RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the World Bank and the International Financial Institutions are providing 
financial assistance for promotion of education; 
(b) if so, the details thereof during the last three years; and 
(c) the details of the achievements made so far in this regard? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HUMAN RESOURCE 
DEVELOPMENT (SHRI MD. ALI ASHRAF FATMI): (a) and (b) The International 
Development Association (World Bank) is providing credit of approximately Rs. 323 
crore and Rs. 1250 crore for implementation of Technician Education Project-Ill (Tech. Ed. 
Ill) and the Technical Educational Qualify Improvement Programme of Government of 
India (TEQIP) respectively. 
The Tech. Ed. Ill project is being implemented in 8 States/Union Territory, namely 
Arunachal Pradesh, Meghayala, Mizoram, Nagaland, Sikkim, Tripura, Jammu & 
Kashmir and Union Territory of Andaman and Nicobar Islands covering 12 existing 
and 9 new polytechnics. 
The TEQIP is being implemented in 13 States, namely Andhra Pradesh, Gujarat, Haryana, 
Himachal Pradesh, Jharkhand, Karnataka, Kerala, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Tamil 
Nadu, Uttar Pradesh, Uttaranchal and West Bengal covering 132 institutions (18 centrally 
funded and 114 States institutions). 
(c) The Tech. Ed. Ill project created annual intake capacity of 740 students in 
new polytechnics, 547 student hostel places in the new -and existing polytechnics, 565 
faculty and staff received content up-gradation, pedagogical hi-tech equipment 
maintenance and utilization training to enhance their efficiency and started 15 new emerging 
technology courses. 
TEQIP will improve efficiency and effectiveness of technical education management 
system in the States and institutions selected under the programme.

Rights of Children 
4081. SHRI C. PERUMAL: Will the Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE 
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
(a) whether India has signed the Charter 'Rights of Children'; 
122 

[2 May, 2005] RAJYA SABHA 
(b) if so, the details thereof; and 
(c) how many of the points in the Charter have been implemented by 
Government and the reasons for not implementing the remaining points? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HUMAN RESOURCE 
DEVELOPMENT (SHRIMATI KANTI SINGH): (a) India acceded to the UN 
convention on the Rights of the Child in 1992 and adopted a National Charter 
for Children in 2004. 
(b) The Convention on the Rights of the Child contains several rights of 
children relating to survival, development and protection. The text of the 
Convention is available at www.unicef.org/crc. 
The National Charter for Children emphasizes Government's commitment to 
children's survival, health and nutrition, standard of living, play and leisure, early 
childhood care, education, protection of the girl child, empowering adolescents, 
equality, life and liberty, name and nationality, freedom of expression, freedom 
of association and peaceful assembly, the right to a family and the right to be 
protected from economic exploitation and all forms of abuse. The Charter 
also provides for protection of children in difficult circumstances, children with 
disabilities, children from marginalized and disadvantaged communities, and 
child victims. It also provides for responsibilities of both parents in rearing their 
children and also provides for ensuring child friendly procedures for the special 
care and protection of children in conflict with law. The text of the Charter is 
available at the website of the Department of Women and Child 
Development at www.wcd.nic.in. 
(c) Rights of the children as enumerated in the Convention on the Rights 
of the Child and the issues of children as contained in the National Charter 
for Children are being addressed in several ways, namely, constitution 
provisions, policies, legislations and several schemes and programmes 
being implemented by different Ministries/Departments and States/UTs. 
The schemes and programmes include Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan, Integrated 
Child Development Services, Reproduc tive and Child Health, Accelerated 
Rural Drinking Water Supply Programme, Central Rural Sanitation 
Programme, Pulse Polio, Integrated Programme for Street Children, 
Integrated Programme for Juvenile Justice, Scheme for elimination of child 
labour, and others.

Lack of publicity of schemes/policies 
4103. SHRI TARIQ ANWAR: Will the Minister of INFORMATION AND 
BROADCASTING be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that Government have failed to give enough publicity to 
various Government Department's Schemes/Policies; 
(b) if so, the reasons therefor; and 
(c) the steps taken in this regard? 
THE MINISTER OF INFORMATION AND BROADCASTING (SHRI S. 
JAIPALREDDY):(a)No, Sir. 
(b) Does not arise. 
(c) Prasar Bharati and all the media units of this Ministry have been 
engaged in disseminating information regarding the policies and programmes 
of the Government among the public. 
Prasar Bharati has given special thrust to disseminating information 
regarding all the Government programmes, including Senior Citizen 
programmes, Consumer Protection, Youth Programmes, Drug Abuse, 
153 

RAJYA SABHA [2 May, 2005] 
Noise Pollution, Women and Child issues, awareness programmes on 
HIV/AIDS, Environment Protection Programmes, New Education Policy, Legal 
Aid and Legal Literacy etc. 
Press Information Bureau (PIB) has launched several media campaigns for 
various departments for the advantage of common man. Social welfare schemes 
like Antyodaya Anna Yojana, Food for Work Programme and other schemes 
related to food security have also been given wide publicity. Special publicity thrust 
was given on important issues and occasions like Literacy Day, Teachers Day, 
Minority Education, Sarva Siksha Abhiyan, Women and Child Development, 
Children Right etc. 
Directorate of Field Publicity (DFP) utilizes inter-personal communication 
to take Government policies to the masses. The Department has carried 
out publicity on issues like national integration, communal harmony, health 
and family welfare, social justi ce and empowerment, human rights and 
child right and rural development.  
Films Division has produced and released films on themes like Mahila 
Samriddhi Yojana, Rojgar Yojana for educated unemployed youth, provision of 
drinking water, national integration, films on health and family welfare, 
panchayati raj, education for all, agricultural policies etc. and films related to 
national integration and nation building. 
DAVP has the mandate to undertake the publicity of the policies of the 
Government Ministries and Department s and brings out printed publicity 
material like posters, brochures, booklets leaflets advertisements in 
newspapers, hoarding, banners, exhibitions for the client Ministries and 
Departments. 
 
Publication Division through its journal Yojana and Kurukshetra have been 
highlighting issues relating to agriculture and rural development, employment 
guarantee etc. Employment News weekly in English, Hindi and Urdu also 
carries articles on major developments issues, employment generation schemes 
etc.

Co-production agreements 
4111. SHRI R. KAMARAJ: Will the Minister of INFORMATION AND 
BROADCASTING be pleased to state: 
158 

[2 May, 2005] RAJYA SABHA 
(a) whether it is a fact that Government had taken a decision to sign Co-
production Agreements with Italy follow ed by France, Germ any, the United 
Kingdom and Singapore for providing liber al shooting conditions abroad at 
subsidized tariffs for Indian film makers; 
(b) if so, the details thereof; 
(c) whether it is also a fact that Government are considering to initiate for a 
policy decision for creation of a single window system for shooting films at 
locations of their choice: and 
(d) if so, the details thereof? 
THE MINISTER OF INFORMATION AND BROADCASTING (SHRI S. 
JAIPAL REDDY): (a) and (b) This Ministry has received proposals from 
certain countries to enter into Audio-visual Co-production Agreements on 
Government to Government basis. Letters of Intent/MoU have been signed with the 
Government of Canada, Italy, China and the United Kingdom expressing the 
intention of the Government to enter into Audio-visual Co-production 
Agreements with each other. 
Entering into such agreements with other countries would enable 
producers of both countries to pool their financial, creative, technical and 
marketing resources, and in providing access to a wider audience base. They 
would also promote higher visibility in international markets for Indian films and 
increased opportunities for the animation sector. 
Entering into Co-production Agreements with other countries would also confer 
to the film produced under such Agreement, the status of a National Production and 
obtain for it all benefits available to a film produced in that country. To that extent 
Indian filmmakers would stand to benefit. While in several countries like United 
Kingdom and Singapore subsidized tariffs are already available for foreign 
filmmakers, there is no specific provision for subsidized tariffs in all cases. 
(c) and (d) Ministry of Information and Broadcasting is the nodal Ministry for 
granting permissions for shooting of foreign feature films/co-productions in India. 
Based on this permission the State Governments/concerned authorities grant 
further permissions. 
In 2004, after detailed inter-ministerial consultations, the guidelines for 
shooting of foreign feature films and co-productions in India have been 
159 

RAJYA SABHA [2 May, 2005] 
liberalized to make them more facilitative. As against twelve weeks taken earlier, 
permission to shoot is now given in three weeks where shooting is in non-
sensitive areas. Further, procedure for script clearance has been streamlined and 
requirement for attachment of a liaison officer with the shooting team and 
preview of the completed film is not mandatory.

Vacancies of SCs/STs in judiciary 
t4130. SHRI RAMADHAR KASHYAP: Will the Minister of LAW AND 
JUSTICE be pleased to state: 
(a) the number of posts lying vacant at various levels as per the 
reservation policy for SCs/STs; 
(b) the steps Government have taken to fill the same; and 
(c) the number of SC/ST Judges appointed in the Supreme Court and High 
Courts? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF LAW AND JUSTICE 
(SHRI K. VENKATAPATHY): (a) to (c) Under article 235 of the Constitution of 
India, the administrative control over the members of subordinate Judicial Service 
vests with the concerned High Court. Further, in exercise of powers conferred 
under proviso to article 309 read the articles 233 and 234 of the Constitution, the 
State Government frames rules and regulations in consultation with the High 
Court. The members of the State Judicial Service are governed by these rules and 
regulations. Therefore, the service conditions, including appointment, promotion 
and reservations etc., of judicial offi cers of the District/Subordinate Courts 
are governed by the respective State Governments. The Central Government is 
not concerned with any of the functions in this regard. 
At the High Court and Supreme Court level, the appointment of the Judges 
of Supreme Court and High Courts are made under articles 124 and 217 of the 
Constitution of India, respectively, which do not provide for reservation for any 
caste or class of persons. No statistics is, therefore, maintained for number of 
Judges belonging to SC/ST/OBCs and minorities. 
The Government have, however, addressed letters to the Chief Ministers of the 
States and the Chief Justices of the High Courts, from time to time, 
requesting them to locate persons from the Bar belonging to Scheduled Castes, 
Scheduled Tribes, other Backward Classes, Minorities and amongst Women who 
are suitable for appointment as High Court Judges.

Creation of corpus for physically challenged persons 
4135. SHRIMATI N.P. DURGA: Will the Minister of SOCIAL JUSTICE 
AND EMPOWERMENT be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that the Supreme Court has ordered Government for 
creation of Rs. 723 crores corpus for the physically challenged persons from 
the excess amount released by Government by way of rounding off the interest 
tax and interest by the banks and other financial institutions from the borrowers 
for the last several years; 
(b) if so, the details thereof; and 
(c) the action that has been taken by Government in this regard? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF SOCIAL JUSTICE 
AND EMPOWERMENT (SHRIMATI SUBBULAKSHMI JAGADEESAN): 
(a) to (c) Yes, Madam, the Hon'ble Supreme Court in CA Nos. 4655 and 5218 
of 2000 decided on 16.4.2004 that the Comptroller and Auditor General of 
India (C&AG) effect recoveries of all the excess amounts realized by the 
Union of India by way of interest tax and interest by the banks and other 
financial institutions and create corpus of such fund for the benefit of the 
disadvantaged people covered by Persons with Disabilities Act, 1995 and the 
National Trust Act, 1999. It has been estimated that the banks had collected 
annually a sum of Rs. 723.79 crores by way of resorting to rounding up of 
the incidence of interest tax. The Court while passing the directions has 
requested the C&AG to manage the trust as Chairman with Finance Secretary and 
Law Secretary of Union of India as ex-officio members. The appellants and other 
banks concerned were also directed to contribute Rs. 50 lakhs to the fund so 
created. The C&AG has filed an application dated 17.8.2004 in the Supreme 
Court seeking modification of the order dated 16.4.2004 as they have 
difficulties in managing the corpus fund.

(a) Yes, Sir. 
(b) The strategies of Special Component Plan for Scheduled Castes (SCs) 
and the Tribal Sub Plan for Scheduled Tribes (STs) have been evolved with the 
objective of ensuring socio economic development of these communities 
through programmes of land reforms, agriculture, animal husbandry, village 
and small industries, small business etc. Special Central Assistance (SCA) is also 
provided to States and UTs implementing Special Component Plan and Tribal 
Sub-Plan which is meant for giving added thrust to the economic development 
programme of these groups. Besides these, three National Finance and Development 
Corporations for Scheduled Castes (NSFDC), Scheduled Tribes (NSTFDC) and for

Government of NCT of Delhi has adopted the following strategy in regard to 
slum/jhuggi dwellers in Delhi since 1990:- 
Where land is required urgently for public purpose, J.J. dwellers are 
relocated at plots cut by DDA/MCD after acquisition of land. Allotment of 18 
sq.mt. plot is made to pre-1990 squatters and 12.5 sq.mt. plot to post-1990 but 
pre-31.12.98 squatters. The allotment is done on licence fee basis. However, 
in-situ upgradation of the J.J. clusters is undertaken where the land owning agency 
gives no objection certificate to the effect that it does not need land in 
foreseeable future. 
The cost of relocation plot is shared as follows: 
* Rs. 44000/- for 18 sq. mt. plot (share of land owning agency-Rs. 
29000/- + plan assistance by Govt, of NCT of Delhi— Rs. 1000/ 
contribution from beneficiaries-Rs. 5000/-) 
* Rs. 35000/- for 12.5 sq. mt. plot (share of land owning agencies-Rs. 
20000/- + plan assistance by Govt, of NCT of Delhi-Rs. 10000/- + 
contribution from beneficiaries - Rs. 5000/-) 
However, the relocation policy of slum/J.J. dwellers in Delhi is sub-judice 
and in a special leave petition filed by the Union of India and Govt, of NCT of 
Delhi against the order dated 29.11.2002 in civil writ petition Nos. 4441/1994 & 
2112/2002 passed by the Delhi High Court setting aside the policy, the Supreme 
Court in its interim orders dated 19.2.2003 and 3.3.2003 stayed the order of the 
Delhi High court and has allowed Government to continue with the existing 
policy and allot land for relocation subject to the result of the petition.

Demand for changes in the admission criteria for nursing courses in the 
country 
SHRI N.K. PREMACHANDRAN (Kerala) : Mr. Deputy Chairman, Sir, 
there is an ample scope for job opportunities for graduates in Nursing both in 
India and foreign countries. But the institutions which conduct nursing courses 
with the recognition of Nursing Council of India restricts the admission to the 
course by imposing certain unwarranted and unnecessary eligibility criteria. In 
the eligibility criteria, it is indicated that only those women who are unmarried 
or legally divorced or widow could apply for this course. So also, height and 
weight are also made as eligibility criteria for admission. 
In the modern era, such unnecessary restriction for applying to the 
Nursing Course is a humiliation to the job-seekers and civilised society as a 
whole. So, it is urged that such unwa rranted and unjustified provisions, if any, 
specified by the Nursing Council of India for admission to the course may be 
deleted to ensure social justice to the women of India. Thank you.

permit repayment of loans without any prepayment premium or refinance the

DR. T. SUBBARAMI REDDY (Andhra Pradesh): Sir, two Independent

Jegurupadu and 208 MW of M/s. SPG L located at Kakinada have been 
funded by a consortium of lenders led by the IDBI in rupees and foreign 
currency. The interest rates for these loans are in the range of 17.5 per cent to

the policy of the State Go vernment is to provide reliable power at an 
affordable tariff rates, the Government of India is requested to give necessary 
instructions to the consortium lenders led by IDBI to permit repayment of loans 
without any prepayment premium or al ternatively that the lenders may 
refinance the outstanding loans, at current  interest rates, ranging from 7 per 
cent to 9 per cent. 
As the matter is of great importanc e and of great help to the State 
Government of Andhra Pradesh, I urge upon the Government of India to

accept the above request of the State Government immediately.   Thank you. 
Demand to amend the Gadgil-Mukherjee Formula 
SHRI SANTOSH BAGRODIA (Rajasthan): Thank you, Mr. Deputy 
Chairman, Sir, for allowing me to speak on a very important subject. Sir, at 
present, Plan assistance to States is governed by the Gadgil-Mukherjee 
formula which, for deciding the quant um of Plan assistance, provides 
weightage to different factors as under:- 
1. Population 60% 
2. Per Capita Income 25% 
3. Performance 7.5% 
(i)       Tax efforts 2.5%  
(ii)      Fiscal management 2%  
(iii)     Population control 1%  
(iv)     Female literacy 1%  
(v)      Completion of ongoing externally 
aided projects 0.5%  
(vi)     Land reforms 0.5%  
4. Special problems 7.5%  
In addition to the above, due weightage needs to be given to the 
following too: 
1. Area : As the cost of delivery of services is more due to larger 
area and low density of population, due weightage for larger area is justified. 
2. Desert : Special weightage on the lines similar to that given to 
hilly States should be given to the St ates like Rajasthan that have 60 per cent 
of its area that is desert. 
3. Index of Infrastructure Development. 
4. Percentage of SC/ST population. 
5. Per capita income and -per capita outlay of Plan compared to 
national average. 
240 

[2 May, 2005] RAJYA SABHA  
6. Lower credit-deposit ratio as compared to the national average. 
7. Investment in the State enterp rises of the Central Government 
situated in the States. 
Now, I would request that the Government of India should give due 
weightage to area, desert, index of infrastructure development, percentage of 
SC/ST population, low credit-deposit ra tio, etc., in the Gadgil-Mukherjee 
formula.   Thank you. 
Demand for early settlment of manpower issue in BSNL 
SHRI PENUMALLI MADHU (Andhra Pradesh): Sir, the Group 'A' 
officers of the Department of Teleco m are being recruited through Combined 
Engineering Services Examination held by the Union Public Service 
Commission. The officers were recruited to the Department of 
Telecommunications with definite recruitment rules and service conditions. 
Subsequently, the Department of Telecommunications has formed two 
corporations, namely, MTNL and BSNL. At the time of forming these 
corporations, all the Group 'A' officers were sent on deemed deputation. There 
are no administrative and management difficulties in achieving the targets set 
by New Telecom Policy with this arrangement. 
It appears that the option for absorbing the Group 'A' officers into 
MTNL and BSNL have been called by changing the rules against which they 
were initially recruited. With this, there is a danger that all the officers may not 
opt for BSNL and MTNL. There is also a danger of losing excellent technical 
manpower in a very vital industry like telecom which has both social and 
economic impact on the society. The se rvices of all these officers may be 
utilised in BSNL/MTNL without changing the rules prevailing as on the date of 
recruitment. 
The whole thing should be thoroughly looked into by the Ministry in 
view of the danger of disruption in the te lecom services mainly in rural, tribal 
and non-remunerative areas where, at present, only BSNL is providing 
services. The question of settling the service matters should be solved 
immediately keeping in view the technical manpower requirement of BSNL. 
241 

RAJYA SABHA [2 May, 2005] 
Demand to expedite issuing of passports by regional passport offices 
in the country 
SHRI V. NARAYANASAMY (Pondicherry): Mr. Deputy Chairman, Sir, 
I thank you for having given me the opportunity to raise this important issue 
relating to the need to expedite issuance of passports in the Regional 
Passport Offices in various parts of th e country. The Ministry of External 
Affairs is controlling the Regional Passport Offices for issuance and renewal of 
passports in various regions of the count ry. The Ministry of External Affairs, 
from time to time, issues instructions to the Regional Passport Offices to issue 
passports in a minimum possible time for the people who apply for new 
passports or for renewal of the old passports. 
But, from the experience and the in formation that is reaching from 
various Regional Passport Offices, we fi nd that there is delay of minimum 
three to six months in issuing passports, in spite of the fact  that the Regional 
Passport Offices have been modernized wi th new technology. People who 
apply for the passports in the Regional  Passport Offices have  been asked to 
visit those places frequently to get the passports. When the people apply for 
their passports in the normal course, they are not getting the passports within 
a period of fifteen days, as per the guidelines issued by the Ministry of 
External Affairs. Due to this delay in issuing the passport by the Regional 
Passport Offices, the peopl e who apply for the passp orts are suffering and 
there is rampant corruption also. This is a very serious matter which the 
Ministry of External Affairs has to look into. 
Therefore, I urge upon the hon. External Affairs Minister to review the 
functioning of Regional Passport Offices and issue fresh guidelines for issuing 
the passports as expeditiously as possible to the people who apply for new 
passports and also who approach them for renewal of passports.

Demand for OBC reservation in Tripura and some other States of 
the country 
SHRI MATILAL SARKAR (Tripura): It is a fact that in as many as 
eight States and Union Territories, there is no reservation facility for the OBC 
people in State-level Services. The reason in most of these St ates is that the 
reservation for the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes has already 
attained the ceiling of 50 per cent in the State Services. The State 
Government cannot go beyond this upper limit owing to the judgement of the 
hon. Supreme Court dated 16 th January 1992, in the case of Indira Sawhney 
and others Vs Union of India and others. A delegat ion from Tripura Legislative 
Assembly submitted a memorandum to the Central Government on 17 th 
August 2001, demanding suitable amendment to Article 16 of the Constitution. 
The then Government turned down'the demand on the ground of a case of 
Tamil Nadu as challenged in the court. In my opinion, the cases of these 
States are different from the cases of  Tamil Nadu. The OBC people of these 
States are entirely out of reservation benefits in State Services. They cannot 
remain denied of their right like this any longer. So, I urge upon the Central 
Government to come forward to do just ice to the OBC people of these States 
by bringing suitable amendment in the Constitution, as early as possible, and 
open out reservation benefits for them in the State Services.  Thank you, Sir.

Demand for early completion of the broad gauge conversion 
trom Trichy to Manamadurai in Tamil Nadu 
DR. K. MALAISAMY (Tamil Nadu): Sir, my Special Mention relates to 
immediate initiative to take up on pr iority of a long-felt need of a BG 
conversion which is postponed or likely to be postponed. 
The long-felt need of the people, not  only from. Tamil Nadu but all 
over the country, to have a direct link  of broad gauge train from Chennai to 
Rameswaram to visit a well-renowned holy place and pilgrim centre, 
Rameswaram, needs no emphasis. Though the scheme of converting the 
existing MG tracks into BG is in vogue for several years, it is a matter of regret 
that Tamil Nadu is still largely lacking  behind in this process. The BG 
conversion beyond Trichy towards Rameswaram, the segment upto 
Manamadurai via Pudukottai is yet to be taken up, though the sanction was 
done long back. 
Now, some disturbing news is heard that the BG conversion from 
Trichy to Manamadurai via Pudukottai is likely to be postponed on the ground 
that the existing MG tracks are required fo r bringing MG coaches/engines   to   
Golden   Rock   Railway   Workshop   for   periodical 
overhauling. 
 
In this connection, it is to be noted that there are already several 
isolated MG sections in the zone, wh ich have no linkage with the workshop, 
and the MG coaches/engines are brought through BG trains. While doing so, 
why should this Trichy-Manamadurai via Pudukottai MG section alone be 
retained? Will it not be arbitrary and discr iminatory? It will amount to scuttling 
the long-felt need for the BG conversion. 
Hence, I request the hon. Minister for Railways to see that the BG 
conversion in question comes through at  any cost dropping the move of 
postponement, if any.

Concern over child labour and their exploitation in the country 
SHRI VIJAY J. DARDA (Maharashtra) : Mr. Deputy Chairman, Sir, on 
6th April, the rescuing of 43 children in embroidery industry is a tip of the 
iceberg. There is a need for concerted efforts to save juveniles caught in such 
Industries. The intricacy involved in t he work requires application of soft and 
flexible fingers. Conservative estimates put a figure of 20,000 children involved 
in such industries in Delhi. Children are trafficked from Bihar as nearly 60 per 
cent of the unit owners come from Sitamarhi region. The unit owners/agents 
convince the fellow villagers to send their children to 'learn' the art of 
embroidery and push them into child labour.   These 
246 

[2 May, 2005] RAJYA SABHA  
children are kept in dingy accommodation and are forced to work daily for 
nearly 18 hours, getting monthly salary of Rs.300. The owners confine these 
children by providing tape-recorders, televisions etc. for entertainment, and 
the nearbjy custom-built dirty dhabas provide frugal non-nutritious food. Such 
pressure-oriented working environment results in several children developing 
orthopaedic and vision-related problems. Thus, after four to five years when 
they grow older and become unfit for the job, they are driven away by 
embroidery owners and replaced by younger and more nimble hands. Despite 
several NGOs working in anti-child labour movement, nothing concrete has 
emerged to prevent organised trafficking of children into the Capital every day; 
and thus, their exploitation continues. Police cannot be oblivious of these 
illegal activities. Thus, concerted efforts by groups, sponsored by the 
Government of India, comprising  compassionate police personnel and 
dedicated social workers with well defined time-bound objectives/targets to be 
achieved, are an immediate necessity to stop this exploitation of children.

SHRIMATI PREMA CARIAPPA (Karnataka): At the outset, I would like to 
congratulate the hon. Minister for his achievements in this Ministry of Environment 
and Forests. Sir, I would like to read out a few lines that I have written. 
Sir, the 42nd Amendment in its Article 48-A to the Directive Principles 
of State Policy has put em phasis on environment stating that, "The State shall 
endeavour to protect and improve the environment and to safeguard the forests and 
wild life of the country." Besides, protection of environment is one of the fundamental 
duties of every citizen of our country. 
Environment pollution and preservation of environment is a burning issue of 
concern not only in India but also all over the world. As such, a comprehensive 
strategy for environmental conservation is the need of the day. Hence, the 
proposed National Environment Policy is a welcome initiative and the very 
essence of N.E.P. is its emphasis on the fact that what is good for the environment 
is also good for the economy. In other words, environmental protection cannot be 
considered in isolation from the development process of the country. This requires 
the use of knowledge already available more effectively for more sustainable 
development rather' than indulge in further research. 
Sir, the adverse impact of deforestation is all visible now. The soils are 
affected by various ailments which have to be treated, followed by 
301 

RAJYA SABHA [2 May, 2005]  
plethora of problems like drought, flash floods, earthquake and soil erosion 
etc. The super cyclone of Orissa, the severe drought in Rajasthan and the 
touching earthquake in Gujarat are a few glaring examples to the after effects 
of large-scale deforestation of the tropical forests. 
Sir, it is indeed an appreciative measure adopted by the Forest 
Department of late though, known as "Participative Approach", with an aim to 
green all barren and degraded lands in rural areas by involving villages both in 
planting as well as protecting and caring the existing forests. This 'Greening 
India Project' even enjoys massive international support. In order to see that it 
does not turn out to be another white elephant, it would be a novel idea to 
start "Krishi Vigyan Kendras" at all districts to reach the grass-root levels. The 
adverse impact of deforestation on the national economy is visible mainly on 
agriculture, and it is far more serious  in India. This requires immediate 
attention of planners and rulers alike. 
Sir, I must bring to the kind attent ion of the Members of this august 
House a new serious problem emerging in my home State, Karnataka - the 
threat of Naxalism and Left-wing extr emism. These Maoist groups have 
almost succeeded in converting the eco-rich Western Ghat, Malnad areas and 
parts of South Canara regions as guerrilla zones. They are attracting tribals, 
dalits and poorer sections of society inhabi tating. in these areas to strengthen 
their base by organising mass move ments. The State Government is 
handicapped due to the lack of adequate la ws to deal with the problem. Even 
Panchayati Raj institutions are not in a position to do  justice to the Naxalite-
affected areas. I am of the firm view that the spread of Naxalism cannot be 
curbed, unless and until development activiti es in favour of the poor, ignorant 
and downtrodden in Naxal-infested areas is taken up in the right earnest. 
Since many of the State Government s are faced with this problem, I 
appeal to the hon. Minister to review the existing forest conservation laws in 
the background of the, need to contain this virus of Naxalism. 
I would like to give a few suggestions. Firstly, the right to give 
environmental clearance to projects should  rest with State Governments, and 
not with the Union Ministry of Environment and Forest, with a view to effective 
governance. Secondly, there should be effective involvement of 'Vana-
Sanrakshana Samithis' to prevent r ed sanders smuggling. Thirdly, major 
problerns,  seriously related to environmental degradation, namely,

population growth, technology and consumption choices and poverty, are to 
be tackled immediately and effectively. Fourthly, the suggestion contained in 
the National Environment Policy regarding the regularisation of encroachment 
on forests is a welcome move, yet, care should be taken to see that it should 
not affect the livelihood of tribals. Fifthly, more and prompt attention should be 
given to forest conservation, taking care to see it does not affect the 
development process in the State adv ersely, in other words, ensure 
sustainable development which is the need of the day. Sixthly, another 
method could be to introduce a tree census programme to have a clear 
picture of number and kinds of trees t hat constitute the natural resources. 
Seventhly, another valid suggestion is th at the children, who are the future of 
the country, should.be given education about environmental protection, which 
are being threatened by human greed, urbanisation, population explosion, etc. 
Sir, keeping all these factors in view , I appeal to the hon. Minister to 
formulate a policy in this regard after peaceful and thorough deliberations. 
Further, it is also very important that both the Cent ral and the State 
Governments should work in a cooper ative spirit rather than adopting a 
confrontational attitude to combat this challenging task ahead. Thank you, Sir.
